question:
Two students discuss why a light ray bends towards the normal when it goes from air into water.

Student P says: “Since the ray bends towards the normal, the speed of light must increase in water. This is why the ray gets pulled closer to the normal.”

Student Q says: “Since the ray bends towards the normal, the speed of light must decrease in water. This is consistent with the wave model of light and was confirmed experimentally.”

Evaluate the two statements in the light of experimental evidence regarding the speed of light in water and air. Give reason.

options.A: Both P and Q are correct because refraction can occur with either increase or decrease of speed depending on the model used.
options.B: P is correct and Q is incorrect because bending towards the normal implies higher speed in the second medium.
options.C: P is incorrect and Q is correct because the speed of light is lower in water than in air, and this experimental result supports the wave explanation of refraction.
options.D: Both P and Q are incorrect because refraction depends only on wavelength change and not on speed.
